hero.title: Cyanotypes
hero.subtitle: One-of-a-kind sun prints, made by hand

categories.name: Botanicals
categories.heading: Botanical Prints
categories.intro: Growing up with a mother who had an encyclopedic knowledge of plant species, and now living in a house filled inside and out with thriving plants, it's no surprise plants found their way into my work. My botanical prints range from close observation to dreamlike compositions of midnight gardens.

categories.name: Animals
categories.heading: Animal Prints
categories.intro: Encounters with animals are often unexpected, joyful moments in nature. This section moves between close study (owls that choose to nest and raise their owlets in my backyard, and jellyfish in the New England Aquarium) and chance encounters, like a fox, a snail, or an iguana crossing my path. Some prints come from patient observation, others from a moment I couldn't have planned for.

categories.name: Things
categories.heading: Things Prints
categories.intro: More than anything, I want my work to elevate everyday objects into art. It could be anything that catches my attention, from my dad's screwdrivers with transparent handles to icicles hanging off my house in the dead of winter. There is so much to see in everyday life. I just try to capture it in a way that lets others see the little moments I do.

categories.name: Places
categories.heading: Places Prints
categories.intro: From my beloved Wellfleet to an abandoned car yard in Tucson, I am inspired by the places I visit and the new things I see there. Places new and familiar push me to notice the beauty around me, and to try to capture it.

categories.name: People
categories.heading: People Prints
categories.intro: One of my very first artistic obsessions (like, when I was 18 months old and drawing scribbles) was the self-portrait. We all love people watching, and that's basically what I do, just in a more lasting way.

categories.name: Mixed Media
categories.heading: Mixed Media Prints
categories.intro: Sometimes even I think just blue isn't enough. I'll add a splash of color, tone a print to a deep brown, or add gold as a counterbalance to all the blue. My mixed media prints are born from a constant desire to experiment and play.
